title: Point transport along the geometric Frobenius of Spec k
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a
prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in the chosen
algebraic closure $\Qlb$, an integer $n\geq1$, and a coefficient ring
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. Put $s=\Spec k$,
$\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed] and
$g_s=\Spec(\gamma):s\to s$, an automorphism of the scheme $s$ with inverse
$\Spec(\gamma^{-1})$. Use the small pro-etale site $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], whose final object is
$(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)$; the inverse image $g_s^{-1}$, defined as
the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of a colimit presheaf
[def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]; for $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E\}$ the
coefficient sheaf $\Lambda_s$, equal to $(A_{E,n})_s$, resp. to the completed
sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_s$
[def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and the structure isomorphism
$c_\Lambda:g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s\to\Lambda_s$, the functor
$g_s^{-1}:D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)\to D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ and
the comparison morphism $\kappa_N:g_s^{-1}N\to Lg_s^*N$ of
[def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] (for $X=Y=s$, $g=g_s$), with
$Lg_s^*$ the derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; the
sections functor $\Gamma(s,-)=(-)(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)$ on
derived categories [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]; and the point
fiber functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], which
for $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E\}$ is $\Gamma(s,-)$ on
$D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility,
def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], for $\Lambda=E$ is
$K\mapsto\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ on
$D^b_c(s,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and for $\Lambda=\Qlb$ is
formed stagewise on $D^b_c(s,\Qlb)$
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] with values in
$D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$ [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. For $N$ in
$D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ the object $Lg_s^*N$ lies again in $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$
([lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] for $\Lambda=A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E$;
for $\Lambda=E,\Qlb$ the operation is the integral one on objects), so
$\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*N)$ is defined.

**$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E\}$.** Let $N$ be a complex of
$\Lambda_s$-modules whose class lies in $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$. Let
$\sigma_N:\Gamma(s,N)\to\Gamma(s,g_s^{-1}N)$ be the map of complexes whose
$i$-th term is the composite
$$
 N^i(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)
 \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{res}_{g_s}\ }
 N^i(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)
 \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{ins}\ }
 (g_s^{-1}N^i)(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s),
$$
where:

* $\operatorname{res}_{g_s}$ is the restriction map of the sheaf $N^i$ along
the morphism $g_s:(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)\to(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)$
of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (a morphism because $\operatorname{id}\circ g_s=g_s$);

* $\operatorname{ins}$ is the coprojection into the colimit
$\varinjlim_{(V,\ s\to s\times_{s,g_s}V)}N^i(V)$, which is the value at
$(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)$ of the presheaf of
[def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] whose sheafification is $g_s^{-1}N^i$, at the
index $V=(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)$ with the $s$-morphism
$(\operatorname{id}_s,\operatorname{id}_s):s\to s\times_{s,g_s}V$, followed by
the value at $(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)$ of the sheafification map
[def-weil-pbc-sheafification].

Both maps commute with the differentials, which are $d^i$ and $g_s^{-1}(d^i)$.
Here $\Gamma(s,N)$ is a complex of $\Lambda$-modules through
$\Lambda\to\Gamma(s,\Lambda_s)$ (constant sections), and
$\Gamma(s,g_s^{-1}N)$ through the same map and the $\Lambda_s$-module
structure of $g_s^{-1}N$ given by $c_\Lambda^{-1}$
[def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]; $\sigma_N$ is $\Lambda$-linear
by [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] (1). The *point transport* is
the morphism of $D(\Lambda)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]
$$
 \iota_N=\Gamma(s,\kappa_N)\circ\sigma_N:\ \operatorname{Fib}_s(N)=\Gamma(s,N)
 \xrightarrow{\ \sigma_N\ }\Gamma(s,g_s^{-1}N)
 \xrightarrow{\ \Gamma(s,\kappa_N)\ }\Gamma(s,Lg_s^*N)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*N).
$$
For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, $\kappa_N$ is the class of the termwise map
$x\mapsto x\otimes1$ into $g_s^*N=g_s^{-1}N\otimes_{g_s^{-1}(A_{E,n})_s}(A_{E,n})_s$,
so $\iota_N$ is the class of a map of complexes. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$,
$Lg_s^*N=R\varprojlim_m\operatorname{Res}_mLg_{s,m}^*(N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,m})$
is a derived limit, not $g_s^{-1}N\otimes^L_{g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s}\Lambda_s$, and
$\kappa_N$ is the map into this derived limit given by part (b) of
[def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison].

**$\Lambda=E$.** An object $N$ of $D^b_c(s,E)$ is an object of
$D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$, with $\operatorname{Fib}_s(N)=\Gamma(s,N)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$
and $Lg_{s,E}^*N=Lg_s^*N$ on objects. Put
$\iota^E_N=\iota^{\mathcal O_E}_N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$, the image of
$\iota^{\mathcal O_E}_N$ under the termwise scalar extension
$-\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E:D(\mathcal O_E)\to D(E)$ (exact, $E$ being flat over
$\mathcal O_E$).

**$\Lambda=\Qlb$.** For an object $(E',K)$ of $D^b_c(s,\Qlb)$, with
$\operatorname{Fib}_s(E',K)=(E',\operatorname{Fib}_sK)$ and
$Lg_s^*(E',K)=(E',Lg_{s,E'}^*K)$, let $\iota_{(E',K)}$ be the morphism of
$D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$ represented at the stage $L=E'$ by
$\iota^{E'}_K:\operatorname{Fib}_sK\to\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_{s,E'}^*K)$.

That, for each $\Lambda$, the $\iota_N$ form a natural transformation
$\iota:\operatorname{Fib}_s\to\operatorname{Fib}_s\circ Lg_s^*$ of functors on
$D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ is [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] (2), and
not part of this definition.

(This is the identification of the fibre at the geometric point $\Spec k$ of
$s$ with the fibre of the transported complex by which $\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$
acts by transport of structure. That $\iota_N$ is an isomorphism is part 1 of
[lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso] and is not part of this
definition.)

source.place: Deligne, La conjecture de Weil II, (1.1.7), pp. 150-151: 'la fibre F-bar de F en le point geometrique Spec(k-bar) ... sur lequel Gal(k-bar/k) agit par transport de structure'; the explicit construction is item 2 of the earlier statement of def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport (worker of def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius), written by an agent

proof.text: The finite-field cardinality gives characteristic p. A distinct prime ell is a unit in the base field, hence in its algebraic closure, all stalks and residue fields.

In the sectionwise inverse-image model, define sigma termwise by restriction along the final-object arrow. Naturality of the constant-sheaf unit and the normalized constant coefficient comparison prove linearity. For completed coefficients, evaluate every limit projection, apply the finite normalization, and use joint injectivity of those projections. Presheaf naturality gives compatibility with the differential and termwise extensionality gives uniqueness. The heterogeneous equality of underlying functions is equivalent to the pointwise section condition. The private restriction-linear-map helper retains successive scalar restrictions rather than converting them to restriction along the composite, avoiding repeated kernel normalization.

Restriction is natural in module maps. Apply full faithfulness of precomposition with localization at quasi-isomorphisms to descend the natural map of section complexes, inserting the standard exact-functor localization comparisons.

Choose a comparison realization inside the proof. Form the natural whole-tower map from the inverse-image diagonal, the reduction unit followed by the diagonal/limit counit, and the inverse-image tower unit. Transpose it under the diagonal/derived-limit adjunction and then the realization isomorphism. The recorded reduction-counit identity and injectivity of adjunction transposition identify the result on every good complex with the recorded Roos comparison. Naturality along a resolution quasi-isomorphism recovers the prescribed inverseImagePullbackComparison for every resolution.

Compose the descended sigma and the natural integral comparison. Naturality gives exactly conjugation of frobeniusPointTransportIntegralComplex by every representing isomorphism. Apply the flat-term K-flat resolution theorem to one representative to force uniqueness. The finite, rational and algebraic-closure definitions retain their original constructions.

proof_origin.place: Deligne Weil II (1.1.7), pp. 150-151. Restriction on constant sections, checked at each finite quotient for completed coefficients. The whole-tower reduction-counit characterization is transposed under the diagonal/limit adjunction to form the natural comparison; exact localization descends sigma and handles every representative and resolution.

split_report.summary: Split by one level. The third map was wrong for O_E: it was defined through g^{-1}N (x)^L_{g^{-1}Lambda} Lambda, while def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom defines the integral Lg^* as the derived limit R lim_m Res_m Lg_m^*(N (x)^L A_{E,m}). The map kappa_N: g_s^{-1}N -> Lg_s^*N is now a new definition node, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison, stated for any isomorphism g of schemes: at finite level the termwise unit x -> x(x)1 into the module inverse image g^*N (which represents Lg^* there), at the integral level the map g^{-1}P -> Cone(1-s)[-1] = Rlim^c_m Res_m g^*(P_m) induced by the compatible maps theta_m, composed with the inverse of g^{-1} of the K-flat resolution P -> N used in def-pur-integral-derived-operations. The point transport is now iota_N = Gamma(s,kappa_N) o sigma_N, with sigma_N = ins o res the map of complexes of the earlier text (restriction along g_s, coprojection into the inverse-image colimit followed by the sheafification map). The cases E and Qlb, previously only 'in the same way', are now explicit: iota^E_N = iota^{O_E}_N (x) E, and at Qlb the class represented at the stage E'. The claims of naturality and Lambda-linearity, previously asserted inside the definition, are split off into the new statement lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural. Added statement dependencies for sheafification (Mathlib leaf def-weil-pbc-sheafification), the sections functor on derived categories, the Qlb target category, the derived category, and lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback (Lg_s^*N lies in D^b_c(s,Lambda), so Fib_s(Lg_s^*N) is defined); def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients is kept. Mathlib has only the categorical ingredients (restriction, colimit coprojection, sheafification, mappingCocone.lift).
